subject: Ledger: sudden p95/p99 spike — KV prefix invalidation suspected
body:
From: Samir Patel <samir@ledger.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-14 09:12 -0700
Subject: URGENT: p95/p99 latency spike and 503s on Hosted API since 08:45

Evelyn / Redwood team,

We're seeing a large regression in tail latency and a spike in 5xx errors starting ~08:45 PDT across our production subsystems. p95 jumped from ~320ms to ~1.6s and p99 to ~3.2s. We also saw a burst of 503s for a subset of requests (mostly chat completions) for tokens coming from our EU and US users.

Attached is a screenshot of our Grafana alert (ledger_grafana_p95_20261014.png) and a short trace where the request stalls waiting on an upstream KV lookup. Can someone confirm if there were any infra/config changes on the hosted path this morning? This is affecting payment flows — need immediate help and an ETA on mitigation.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Reliability, Ledger Inc

---

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@ledger.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-14 09:25 -0700
Subject: Re: URGENT: p95/p99 latency spike and 503s on Hosted API since 08:45

Hi Samir — thanks for the alert and the Grafana screenshot. I'm escalating to our on-call infra and runtime leads (cc'd). We're treating this as P0.

Initial asks so we can triage faster:
- Any specific request IDs or example payloads?
- Is the traffic mostly to text generation / chat endpoints?
- Can you confirm the earliest observed spike time (yourdashboard shows ~08:45 but confirm with traces)?

We will validate recent deploys/config changes and check whether there was a cache invalidation job or TTL change. I will keep you updated every 30 minutes until stable.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@ledger.com>
Date: 2026-10-14 09:32 -0700
Subject: Fwd: URGENT: p95/p99 latency spike — possible KV/prefix cache issue (Ledger)

Dylan/Marissa — Samir reports p95/p99 spikes and some 503s starting 08:45 PDT. They attached a trace showing a stalled upstream KV lookup.

Context: we rolled out a small config change to the hosted cache invalidation service at 08:40 that tightened prefix TTLs and added a zero-ttl invalidation path for a small customer cohort. I flagged it as low-risk but didn't realize it would touch global invalidation semantics.

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm whether the 08:40 config change created a mass invalidation or accidental wildcard eviction?
- If so, can we rollback the change ASAP and trigger controlled prefix warmup for Ledger prefixes?
- If rollback isn't instant, can we route Ledger traffic to a fallback model variant or a dedicated pool to mitigate customer impact?

Please priority-P0. I'll keep Ledger on the thread and coordinate customer updates.

On Thu, Oct 14, 2026 at 09:12 AM Samir Patel <samir@ledger.com> wrote:
> Evelyn / Redwood team,
> 
> We're seeing a large regression in tail latency... [trimmed]

—Evelyn

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@ledger.com>
Date: 2026-10-14 09:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: URGENT: p95/p99 latency spike — possible KV/prefix cache issue (Ledger)

Quick update from on-call infra: preliminary root cause looks like a mass prefix invalidation triggered by the 08:40 config change. The invalidation code path incorrectly treated some customer-specific prefixes as a wildcard, causing widespread KV evictions across hosted nodes. That created a thundering-herd as many requests missed the cache at once and attempted synchronous KV fills, which pushed the upstream stores and increased request latencies and 503s.

Actions taken (09:50 local):
- Rolled back the 08:40 config change (rollback_patch.diff attached).
- Throttled the invalidation queue so backend stores can recover and avoid cascading timeouts.
- Started a warmup job (warmup_script.sh) targeted at Ledger prefixes to repopulate local KV caches in the affected pools.
- Temporarily increased served capacity in the affected hosted pool for us-west-2 to absorb the load.
- Proposed a short-term per-API-key soft-rate limit for Ledger to reduce pressure on upstream while we warm caches (awaiting product approval).

Observed impact: after the rollback we saw test traffic p95 for a synthetic Ledger trace fall from ~1.6s to ~320ms within ~6 minutes of the rollback. We'll monitor live traffic and post metrics to the incident Jira.

Attaching cache_eviction_log_20261014.txt for traces and error frequencies.

—Dylan
SRE On-Call, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@ledger.com>
Date: 2026-10-14 10:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: URGENT: p95/p99 latency spike — possible KV/prefix cache issue (Ledger)

Status update for Ledger: rollback completed at 09:50 and warmup started immediately. Live metrics show p95 trending back to normal for Ledger test traffic.

Next steps for containment and customer care:
- Continue warmup for next 2 hours and monitor p95/p99, error rates, and throughput.
- Run a postmortem; INV ticket created: INF-8721 (link in thread).
- Recommend we offer Ledger 1 week of service credit for the disruption and an assisted warm-up for any future planned invalidations. Rishi/Tessa: please advise on the credits/PR.
- Add explicit guardrails in the cache invalidation path (no wildcard invalidations without explicit approval).

Samir — can you confirm whether any retries from your side caused additional load? We'll cross-check request patterns.

—Marissa
Director, Runtime & Serving, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@ledger.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-14 15:43 -0700
Subject: Re: URGENT: p95/p99 latency spike — possible KV/prefix cache issue (Ledger)

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We've seen production latency and 5xx rates drop back to baseline since ~11:00. We had a handful of payment failures during the window but nothing catastrophic — still investigating.

We will expect a postmortem and formal SLA credit request. Please include the timeline and the exact config patch that caused the issue. We appreciate the rollback and the warmup effort; Rishi, Samir (cc Evelyn) — I'd like a short call tomorrow for follow-up and to discuss guardrails.

Samir
